# Weekend drinking

In the first part of this class activity, we work with survey data from 77 college students on a dry campus (i.e., alcohol is prohibited) in the US. The survey asks students “How many alcoholic drinks did you consume last weekend?” The data includes the following variables:

* `drinks`: the number of drinks the student reports consuming
* `sex`: an indicator for whether the student identifies as male (1 = male)
* `OffCampus`: an indicator for whether the student lives off campus (1 = off campus, 0 = on campus)
* `FirstYear`: an indicator for whether the student is a first-year student (1 = first year, 0 = not first year)

## The model

To account for excess zeros in the data, we fit a *zero-inflated Poisson* (ZIP) model. Here is the probability function for our model:

$$P(Y_i = y | \mathbf{x}_i) = \begin{cases} e^{-\lambda_i}(1 - p_i) + p_i & y = 0 \\ \dfrac{e^{-\lambda_i} \lambda_i^y}{y!}(1 - p_i) & y > 0 \end{cases}$$

where

$$
\begin{aligned}
\log \left( \frac{p_i}{1 - p_i} \right) &= \mathbf{x}_i^T \boldsymbol{\gamma} \\
\log(\lambda_i) &= \mathbf{x}_i^T \boldsymbol{\beta}
\end{aligned}
$$

## Model output

```{r include=F}
library(pscl)
library(tidyverse)

wdrinks <- read.csv("../class_activities/weekendDrinks.csv")

FirstYear <- ifelse( wdrinks$dorm %in% c("mohn","kittlesby", "kildahl"), "TRUE", "FALSE")
OffCampus <- ifelse( wdrinks$dorm == "off campus", "TRUE", "FALSE")

wdrinks <- cbind(wdrinks, FirstYear, OffCampus)
```

```{r}
m1 <- zeroinfl(drinks ~ sex + FirstYear + OffCampus, 
               dist = "poisson", data = wdrinks)

summary(m1)
```

1. What is the estimated probability that a female first-year student who lives on campus never drinks?
